h1:
Rayong for Photographers
3 Days to Fill Your Feed
intro: If you're coming to Rayong mainly to shoot for social, this is the route we'd start with. Three days take you from the wooden boardwalk through the Golden Mangrove Field, to the HTMS Prasae warship memorial that looks cinematic from any angle, and finally to Sai Kaew Beach and Ao Phrao on Koh Samet. We timed each stop to land in its best light, and we list real entry and boat fees so you're not guessing once you arrive.

blocks.html: Rayong is under three hours' drive from Bangkok, but it packs a lot of different photo backdrops into a small area: bright green mangrove forest, an old warship by the sea, and white-sand island beaches. We built this plan specifically for people who care about photos, hitting each spot when the light works for it instead of showing up at random and ending up shooting into the sun.

items: Day 1 — Pak Nam Prasae: Golden Mangrove Field + HTMS Prasae warship memorial + Prasaesin Bridge (midday–evening scenes)
Day 2 — Koh Samet: boat from Ban Phe, then Sai Kaew Beach, the mermaid statue, and Ao Phrao at sunset
Day 3 — Around town: Mae Ramphueng Beach, a seaside café, then head home

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Pak Nam Prasae — Golden Mangrove Field, the warship, Prasaesin Bridge

items.activity: Leave Rayong town for Pak Nam Prasae, Klaeng district
items.note: It's about an hour's drive, or roughly 3.5 hours if you're coming straight from Bangkok, so we start the first day a little late on purpose.

items.activity: Walk the Golden Mangrove Field boardwalk
items.note: The wooden walkway runs about 2.7 km through the mangroves. It's free and open 6:00 AM–6:00 PM. The Prong leaves catch the sun and turn golden best from around 11:00 AM–3:00 PM, right when you arrive.

items.activity: Lunch in the Pak Nam Prasae community
items.note: There are seafood places and riverside community spots around here. After eating, stroll the old waterfront cultural street for some everyday-life shots.

A decommissioned warship set up as a seaside memorial. Entry is free, open roughly 7:00 AM–6:30 PM. You can walk onto the ship and shoot the bow, the deck, and the hull's frame against the sky for a really cinematic feel. Some of the Golden Mangrove boardwalk routes end near here too.

items.activity: Prasaesin Bridge for the evening light
items.note: The bridge crosses the Prasae River, with the community on one side and open sea on the other. It's a good spot to catch the golden hour before heading back to your room.

blocks.title: Day 1 tip
blocks.html: The Golden Mangrove Field only really glows when there's sun. On an overcast day the leaves read as deep green rather than gold, so check the forecast before you head out, and wear shoes that are comfortable for a long walk on the boardwalk.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Koh Samet — Sai Kaew Beach, the mermaid, Ao Phrao

items.activity: Head to Ban Phe pier and catch the boat to Koh Samet
items.note: A regular ferry runs about 100 THB round trip, while a speedboat is around 250–300 THB per trip. The crossing takes no more than 40 minutes, and you can leave your car on the Ban Phe side.

items.activity: Enter the national park, then head straight to Sai Kaew Beach
items.note: Park entry is 40 THB for Thais and 200 THB for foreigners, half price for kids. Sai Kaew Beach has fine white sand running about 800 meters and is the main beach that's easiest to shoot.

items.activity: Shoot the mermaid statue at the end of Sai Kaew Beach
items.note: The beach's signature landmark, the statue faces out to sea. In the late morning the sun isn't too harsh yet, so you get the blue sea behind it and fewer people than in the afternoon.

items.activity: Lunch by the beach, then a swim break
items.note: There are plenty of restaurants to choose from along Sai Kaew Beach. The midday sun is strong, so it's better to take a break than to be out shooting.

items.activity: Move over to Ao Phrao on the west side for sunset
items.note: Ao Phrao is quieter and more private, with rocks to shoot around, and it's known as the best sunset spot on the island. Get there about half an hour before the golden hour so you can time it well.

blocks.title: Koh Samet tip
blocks.html: If you want an empty beach with few people in the frame, shoot in the late morning before 11. Or, if you stay one night on the island, you get both the Ao Phrao sunset and a quiet beach in the early morning.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Around town — Mae Ramphueng Beach, a seaside café

items.activity: Morning walk and shoot at Mae Ramphueng Beach
items.note: A long, continuous beach right in Rayong town. The morning sky is still soft and there are few people, so it's easy to shoot minimal sea-and-sand frames.

items.activity: Sit at a seaside café around Mae Ramphueng or Ban Phe
items.note: This area has several sea-view cafés. Grab a coffee-cup-against-the-sea shot to close out the trip before heading back.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs at Ban Phe, then head home
items.note: Ban Phe market has dried seafood and souvenirs to choose from before you start the drive back to Bangkok.

blocks.text: What to pack as a photographer

items: Power bank — shooting all day drains your battery fast, especially on the island where charging spots are hard to find
Lens cloth — sea spray and mangrove humidity smudge the lens easily
Solid-color outfits — they stand out against the green of the mangroves and the blue of the sea better than busy patterns
Sunscreen and a hat — there's no shade at all on the sea or on the boardwalk through the field

faq.q: When is the Golden Mangrove Field best for photos?
faq.a: The Prong leaves catch the sun and look most golden from around 11:00 AM–3:00 PM when there's full sun. On an overcast day the leaves read as deep green instead. It's free and open every day 6:00 AM–6:00 PM.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for the HTMS Prasae warship memorial?
faq.a: It's free, no entry fee, open roughly 7:00 AM–6:30 PM every day. It's in Pak Nam Krasae, Klaeng district. You can walk onto the ship to take photos, and it's close to the Golden Mangrove Field, so you can do both in one day.

faq.q: How much are the boat and entry fees for Koh Samet?
faq.a: A regular ferry from Ban Phe pier is about 100 THB round trip, and a speedboat is around 250–300 THB per trip, with the crossing taking no more than 40 minutes. Park entry is 40 THB for Thais and 200 THB for foreigners, half price for kids.

faq.q: Where's the best place to shoot the sunset on Koh Samet?
faq.a: Ao Phrao on the west side is known as the best sunset spot on the island, with rocks to shoot around, and it's quieter and more private than Sai Kaew Beach. We'd suggest getting there about half an hour before the golden hour.

faq.q: Can this plan be done in 2 days?
faq.a: Yes. If you're short on time, combine Day 1 with the around-town stops into a single day, leaving the other day for Koh Samet. It'll be a bit rushed and you'll miss the best light at a few spots, though. If you want the full set of shots, we'd suggest the 3-day plan as is.
